data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD and install scripts contain standard, benign packaging logic with pinned checksums and no malicious code execution. The disagreement was solely caused by an API error (HTTP 400) in the Qwen model when auditing the .SRCINFO metadata file, which incorrectly cascaded to an inconclusive overall verdict. DeepSeek successfully audited all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The Qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 error when attempting to audit .SRCINFO, marking it as inconclusive and causing the final verdict to be inconclusive. DeepSeek successfully audited .SRCINFO and found it safe. Since .SRCINFO is non-executable metadata, the API failure should not have resulted in an inconclusive security verdict for the package.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to audit .SRCINFO due to an HTTP 400 API error.
learnings: API errors or tool failures when auditing non-executable metadata files (like .SRCINFO) should not cascade to an 'inconclusive' overall security verdict. The tool should either retry, ignore metadata file failures if executable files are safe, or clearly separate tool errors from security verdicts.
